accepted.label: Loading and exploring NLTK's Portuguese text corpora
accepted.description: How to import and access NLTK's built-in Portuguese corpora, including the examples module, Machado de Assis works, and the MacMorpho tagged corpus, to retrieve text, words, and tagged words.
coverage_criteria: Imports a Portuguese corpus like nltk.corpus.machado.
Lists file IDs and retrieves raw text or words for a file.
For MacMorpho, accesses tagged_words and distinguishes between words and tagged tokens.
accepted.merge_rationale: These candidates all demonstrate the same pattern of importing a specific NLTK corpus and querying its contents, differing mainly in the corpus name and whether tags are present. They collectively teach how to access Portuguese language resources.

accepted.label: Working with the Floresta treebank
accepted.description: How to access the Floresta Portuguese treebank, simplify its complex part-of-speech tags, and retrieve parsed syntactic trees.
coverage_criteria: Imports nltk.corpus.floresta and lists words or tagged words.
Writes a function to simplify tags (e.g., 'H+n' to 'n').
Accesses parsed_sents() and can explain that they represent syntactic structure.
accepted.merge_rationale: Both candidates focus on the same treebank, teaching complementary aspects: tag manipulation and parsed sentence access.

accepted.label: Searching text with NLTK's built-in and regex methods
accepted.description: Using NLTK's concordance, similar, collocations, and findall with regex to locate words and analyze their contexts.
coverage_criteria: Uses concordance() to display a word in context.
Uses similar() to find words with similar distribution.
Uses collocations() to extract frequent multi-word expressions.
Applies findall() with a regex pattern to search text.
accepted.merge_rationale: These candidates cover different search tools in NLTK that together form a coherent set of methods for exploring text content, from simple concordances to regex pattern matching.

accepted.label: Tokenization with NLTK
accepted.description: Understanding tokenization as converting text into a list of words and punctuation, and using nltk.word_tokenize for better handling of contractions than simple regex splitting.
coverage_criteria: Recognizes that NLTK represents tokenized text as a list of string tokens.
Uses nltk.word_tokenize to split a sentence with contractions and explains why it is advantageous.
accepted.merge_rationale: These two candidates cover the concept of tokenization from both a representational perspective and a specific function that improves tokenization quality.

accepted.label: Analyzing tokenized text with NLTK and Python
accepted.description: Performing basic text analysis operations on tokenized lists, including extracting unique vocabulary, filtering/transforming tokens with list comprehensions, computing frequency distributions, and finding n-grams containing a target word.
coverage_criteria: Uses set() and sorted() to obtain the unique vocabulary of a tokenized text.
Writes a list comprehension to filter tokens by length or case.
Creates a FreqDist and retrieves the most frequent words.
Generates n-grams and filters those containing a specific word, displaying the most frequent.
accepted.merge_rationale: These candidates represent a sequence of progressively advanced manipulations on token lists, all essential for exploratory text analysis.

accepted.label: Handling Portuguese text encoding (ISO 8859-1)
accepted.description: Awareness that many Portuguese text resources use ISO 8859-1 encoding and how to decode such text in Python when reading files.
coverage_criteria: Explains why specifying encoding is necessary when opening Portuguese text files.
Decodes bytes using 'ISO 8859-1' encoding in Python.
accepted.merge_rationale: This candidate is a standalone practical detail about text encoding that is specific to Portuguese character sets.

accepted.label: Implementing a custom concordance tool
accepted.description: Writing a Python function that searches for a word in a list of sentences and prints it with surrounding context, mimicking NLTK's concordance.
coverage_criteria: Defines a function that takes a word and context width, iterates over tokenized sentences, and prints formatted concordance lines.
accepted.merge_rationale: This candidate is a self-contained programming task that deepens understanding of text indexing and formatting.

accepted.label: Stemming with Porter Stemmer in NLTK
accepted.description: Using the Porter Stemmer algorithm to reduce words to their stems through rule-based suffix stripping.
coverage_criteria: Applies PorterStemmer to a list of words and observes the stemmed outputs.
Explains that stemmed outputs may not be real words (e.g., 'generously' -> 'gener').
accepted.merge_rationale: This candidate covers a specific stemming algorithm, which is a fundamental text normalization technique.

accepted.label: Snowball Stemmer for multilingual stemming
accepted.description: Snowball Stemmer is a stemming algorithm supporting multiple languages, often more accurate than Porter Stemmer. Use it to reduce words to their stems.
coverage_criteria: List several languages supported by SnowballStemmer.
Initialize SnowballStemmer with a language and stem a word.
Explain why Snowball Stemmer might be preferred over Porter Stemmer.
accepted.merge_rationale: Single candidate; standalone concept for NLTK stemming with Snowball.

accepted.label: Lemmatization with WordNetLemmatizer
accepted.description: WordNetLemmatizer reduces words to dictionary form using WordNet. Unlike stemming, lemmas are actual words. Requires downloading wordnet corpus.
coverage_criteria: Explain the difference between lemmatization and stemming.
Instantiate WordNetLemmatizer and lemmatize a word.
Identify that lemmatization depends on a lexical database like WordNet.
accepted.merge_rationale: Single candidate; standalone concept for NLTK lemmatization.

accepted.label: Processing text and exploring documents, tokens, and spans in spaCy
accepted.description: Use spacy.blank to create a pipeline and process text into a Doc. Understand tokenization as the process of splitting text into tokens. Access tokens by index and create spans.
coverage_criteria: Write code to create a blank Portuguese pipeline, process 'Olá mundo', and confirm the result is a Doc.
Given a Doc for 'três cachorros e dois gatos', retrieve the first token and create a span for 'três cachorros'.
Define tokenization and explain that spaCy's tokenizer is language-specific, giving examples.
accepted.merge_rationale: These candidates cover the practical steps of initializing spaCy, processing text, and understanding the resulting document structure, along with the concept of tokenization. They form a single foundational workflow.

accepted.label: Using lexical attributes for pattern detection
accepted.description: Token attributes like `like_num` can identify numeric tokens. Combine attributes to find patterns such as percentages.
coverage_criteria: Explain how to find tokens that represent numbers using `like_num`.
Write a loop to detect a number followed by a '%' sign.
accepted.merge_rationale: Single candidate; standalone technique for lexical pattern detection.

accepted.label: Loading and understanding pre-trained spaCy models
accepted.description: Load pre-trained pipelines with spacy.load. Understand model packages (config, weights, strings.json) and trade-offs between blank and pre-trained models of different sizes.
coverage_criteria: Write code to load the Portuguese small pipeline and process a text, printing the Doc's text.
List what is included in a spaCy pipeline package and explain why training data is not needed.
Explain the difference between blank and pre-trained models, and compare speed/accuracy trade-offs of model sizes.
accepted.merge_rationale: These candidates all relate to the nature and usage of pre-trained spaCy models: what they contain, how to load them, and the different types available.

accepted.label: Predicting part-of-speech tags and dependencies
accepted.description: After processing text with a trained pipeline, each token has a .pos_ (coarse POS tag) and .dep_ (dependency label).
coverage_criteria: Given a Doc from a Portuguese pipeline, write a loop to print each token's text, .pos_, and .dep_.
accepted.merge_rationale: Single candidate; focused on two specific annotation types that are commonly used together.

accepted.label: Named entity recognition and manual correction
accepted.description: Trained pipelines identify named entities (doc.ents). When predictions miss an entity, manually create a Span for the missed tokens.
coverage_criteria: Iterate over doc.ents printing entity text and label, and use spacy.explain to describe a label.
When a model fails to recognize 'iPhone X', write code to create a Span for those two tokens.
accepted.merge_rationale: Manual correction is a practical complement to NER; teaching them together gives a complete view of entity handling.

accepted.label: Rule-based matching with Matcher
accepted.description: Use the Matcher class to define token-based patterns with attributes and operators for finding sequences in text.
coverage_criteria: Write code to initialize a Matcher, add a pattern that matches 'iPhone X', apply it to a Doc, and print matched spans.
Write patterns using lemmas, POS tags, and quantifiers (e.g., '+', '*', '?') to match flexible sequences.
accepted.merge_rationale: Basic and complex pattern writing are a natural progression of the same tool; they form one concept of using Matcher for rule-based matching.

accepted.label: Introduction to Natural Language Processing (NLP)
accepted.description: NLP is the field of making computers understand natural language, relying on statistical approximations; applications include information extraction and chatbots.
coverage_criteria: Explain that NLP deals with understanding natural language by machines.
Mention that approaches are statistical and approximate.
Give examples of applications such as document information extraction or chatbots.
accepted.merge_rationale: Single candidate; foundational concept providing context for text processing tools.

accepted.label: Overview of spaCy as a production-ready NLP library
accepted.description: spaCy is an open-source MIT-licensed NLP library, maintained by Explosion.ai, supporting 73 languages and focused on production with pre-trained models.
coverage_criteria: Identify spaCy as a production-focused NLP library.
Differentiate spaCy from other libraries like NLTK (academic).
State that it supports multiple languages and offers small, medium, and large pre-trained models.
accepted.merge_rationale: Single candidate; library overview necessary before using spaCy.

accepted.label: Contêineres spaCy: Doc, Token e Span
accepted.description: No spaCy, um Doc representa o documento inteiro processado, contendo uma sequência de objetos Token. Um Span é uma fatia de um Doc. Esses contêineres são a base para navegar e acessar atributos linguísticos.
coverage_criteria: Explicar o que é um Doc e como criá-lo.
Descrever Token como uma unidade individual com atributos.
Demonstrar como criar um Span usando slicing.
accepted.merge_rationale: Conceito individual representando os contêineres básicos do spaCy.

accepted.label: Atributos de tokens no spaCy: text, shape_ e is_alpha
accepted.description: Cada token possui atributos como .text, .shape_ e .is_alpha que descrevem sua forma e tipo, permitindo filtrar ou identificar padrões no texto.
coverage_criteria: Listar e definir os atributos text, shape_ e is_alpha.
Fornecer um exemplo de uso de shape_.
Usar is_alpha para separar palavras de pontuação ou números.
accepted.merge_rationale: Conceito individual sobre atributos básicos de tokens no spaCy.

accepted.label: POS tagging – classificação gramatical dos tokens
accepted.description: POS tagging atribui a cada token uma classe gramatical (ex.: substantivo, verbo). No spaCy, usa-se .pos_ (como NOUN, VERB) e .tag_ para detalhes mais granulares.
coverage_criteria: Explicar o que é POS tagging.
Extrair tags POS de uma frase com .pos_.
Identificar tags como PROPN, VERB em exemplos.
accepted.merge_rationale: Conceito individual sobre análise gramatical com spaCy.

accepted.label: Lematização – redução à forma canônica
accepted.description: Lematização transforma palavras flexionadas em sua forma base (ex.: 'faz' → 'fazer'). No spaCy, acessa-se via .lemma_. Diferencia-se de stemming, que apenas corta radicais.
coverage_criteria: Definir lematização e diferenciar de stemming.
Obter o lema de um token com .lemma_.
Dar um exemplo de lematização como 'comprou' → 'comprar'.
accepted.merge_rationale: Conceito individual sobre lematização no spaCy.

accepted.label: Análise de dependências sintáticas (dep_)
accepted.description: A análise de dependências atribui a cada token um rótulo .dep_ indicando sua função sintática (ex.: nsubj para sujeito, obj para objeto). Permite visualizar a estrutura da frase com displacy.
coverage_criteria: Explicar o que .dep_ representa.
Identificar o nsubj de um verbo em uma frase.
Usar displacy.render para visualizar dependências.
accepted.merge_rationale: Conceito individual sobre análise sintática com spaCy.

accepted.label: Reconhecimento de Entidades Nomeadas (NER) no spaCy
accepted.description: NER identifica entidades como pessoas, organizações, locais no texto. No spaCy, acessível via doc.ents, com atributos como .label_ (PERSON, ORG, etc.).
coverage_criteria: Definir NER e listar tipos de entidades.
Extrair entidades com doc.ents.
Imprimir texto e label de cada entidade.
accepted.merge_rationale: Conceito individual sobre NER no spaCy.
